You are reverse-engineering a Python program's behavior as a BLACK BOX by running a precompiled executable.

Executable: /workspace/dataset/test12_executable
Source (Python, for reference):
    import argparse
    from furl import furl
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--d', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    f = furl(args.a)
    print(f.fragment.__setattr__('str', args.b) or f.fragment)   # LINE1
    print(f.fragment.add(args.c))                                # LINE2
    print(f.fragment.set(args.d, 'value'))                       # LINE3
    print(f.url)                                                 # LINE4

RUN IT LIKE: /workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a "<A>" --b "<B>" --c "<C>" --d "<D>"
Never use the 'python' command. Do not read furl source; it is not available. Probe empirically.

ALREADY-ESTABLISHED FACTS (do not re-derive, but DO stress-test if in your area):
- --b is completely ignored: __setattr__('str', b) sets a dead instance attribute, no effect, returns None.
- LINE1 prints str(fragment) as parsed from A.
- LINE2 = fragment.path.add(C) then print str(fragment).
- LINE3 = fragment.path.load(D); fragment.query.load('value'); print str(fragment)  -> query is always literally 'value'.
- LINE4 prints the whole URL with the mutated fragment.
- Fragment str = path + '?' + query when both non-empty, else path+query. When query non-empty, literal '?' chars inside the fragment PATH are escaped to %3F; when query is empty they stay raw.
- furl DECODES percent-escapes on parse and RE-ENCODES on output: '%41%42' -> 'AB'; '%2F' inside a path segment -> stays '%2F'; lone '%' -> '%25'; 'a%zz' -> 'a%25zz'.
- Scheme and host are lowercased. Default ports dropped (http:80, https:443) but non-default kept (http:443 kept).
- URL query: '+' decodes to space, space encodes to '+'. 'a=b&c&d=' round-trips exactly (key-only 'c' vs empty-value 'd=' are distinct).

METHOD: run MANY probes (60+), vary one thing at a time, use printf %q or cat -A style to make whitespace visible, and note exit codes and stderr separately. Prefer a bash loop over a case list.

DELIVERABLE: a precise, implementable specification of YOUR assigned area: exact algorithm/rules, character sets (list the literal safe characters), ordering of operations, and a table of at least 25 concrete input->output examples you actually observed (verbatim). Call out anything surprising or that you could not determine. Be rigorous: an implementer will code directly from your spec with no access to the executable.


AREA UNDER AUDIT: fragment-compose

Another agent produced these RULES for this area:
R1. PARSE (Fragment.load). The fragment source text is everything after the FIRST '#' in A (a later '#' belongs to the fragment text itself and is later encoded as %23). If A has no '#', the fragment source is ''. Splitting the fragment source into (path, query) uses this exact algorithm, operating on the RAW, still-percent-encoded text:
  toks = frag.split('?', maxsplit=1)   # at most 2 pieces
  if len(toks) == 1:                    # no '?' anywhere
      if '=' in frag: query.load(frag); path.load('')      # whole thing is the QUERY
      else:           path.load(frag);  query.load('')     # whole thing is the PATH
  else:                                 # there is at least one '?'
      if '=' in toks[1]: path.load(toks[0]); query.load(toks[1])   # split at the first '?'
      else:              path.load(frag); query.load('')           # NO split; the '?' stays inside the PATH
R2. The '=' test is performed on the RAW text before any percent-decoding. '%3D' is NOT an '='. Evidence: '#a%3Db' -> path='a=b' (decoded only afterwards; L2 appends '/c' to it), whereas '#a=b' -> query='a=b' (L2 gives 'c?a=b'). Likewise '#a?b%3Dc' has no '=' in toks[1]='b%3Dc', so the whole 'a?b%3Dc' becomes the path.
R3. maxsplit is exactly 1, verified by '#a?b?c=d': toks[1]='b?c=d' contains '=' so path='a', query='b?c=d' (rendered 'a?b%3Fc=d'). A plain split('?') would have given toks[1]='b' (no '='), i.e. path='a?b?c=d' — not what happens.
R4. Consequences worth memorizing: a fragment that is only '?' -> path='?', query='' (NOT an empty split). '#??' -> path='??'. '#?&' -> path='?&'. '#a?' -> path='a?'. '#a?b' -> path='a?b'. '#?q=1' -> path='', query='q=1'. '#?=' -> path='', query='='. '#=' -> path='', query='='. '#a=b?c' -> path='a=b?c' (toks[1]='c' has no '='). '#a=b?c=d' -> path='a=b', query='c=d'.
R5. COMPOSE (str(fragment)). Let p = str(fragment.path) rendered with the fragment-path encoder (so a literal '?' in the path has already been encoded to '%3F', '#'->'%23', ' '->'%20', '%'->'%25'), and q = str(fragment.query) rendered with the query encoder (' '->'+', '?'->'%3F'). Then:
  if q == '':  return p.replace('%3F', '?')      # un-escape '?' – unambiguous with no query
  if p == '':  return q                          # NO leading '?' separator
  return p + '?' + q
R6. Equivalently as a 2x2 table: (path='', query='') -> ''; (path=P, query='') -> P with every '%3F' turned back into a literal '?'; (path='', query=Q) -> Q verbatim, with no '?' prefix; (path=P, query=Q) -> P + '?' + Q with '?' inside P kept as '%3F'.
R7. The '%3F' -> '?' un-escaping in the query-empty case is applied to the FINAL ENCODED path string, not to the decoded segments. Proof: C='a?b%3Dc' appended to path 'z' gives 'z/a%3Fb%253Dc' when the fragment query is non-empty, but 'z/a?b%253Dc' when it is empty — the '%3F' produced by the path encoder is rewritten while the neighbouring '%25' is untouched. Implement it literally as encoded_path.replace('%3F','?') (the encoder always emits uppercase hex, so a case-insensitive replace is unnecessary).
R8. Only '?' gets this special treatment. '#' stays '%23' in both cases, '%' stays '%25', ' ' stays '%20'. Verified by an exhaustive ASCII 33..126 sweep: the query-empty and query-non-empty renderings of the fragment path are byte-identical for all 94 printable characters EXCEPT '?' ('x?y' vs 'x%3Fy').
R9. '?' characters that live in the fragment QUERY are always percent-encoded to %3F, regardless of whether the path is empty. '#??=' -> path='', query has key '?' -> output '%3F='. '#a?b?c=d' -> 'a?b%3Fc=d'. There is never a case where a '?' inside the query is emitted raw.
R10. SEPARATOR FLAG. furl's Fragment has a `separator` attribute, but it is NOT observable through this program. Every LINE3 output in ~40 different A values (including path-only fragments such as '#a', '#/', '#?', '#a?', and no-fragment URLs) is 'd?value' — i.e. the '?' separator is emitted whenever both path and query are non-empty. Implement str(fragment) as if separator is permanently True; do not model it.
R11. LINE1 = str(fragment) as parsed from A (composition rule above). LINE2 = fragment.path.add(C) then str(fragment); the query parsed from A is preserved, so LINE2 exercises the (non-empty path, non-empty query) branch when A's fragment had a query. LINE3 = fragment.path.load(D); fragment.query.load('value'); then str(fragment) — the query is ALWAYS the literal 'value', so LINE3 is 'value' when D produces an empty path and '<encoded D>?value' otherwise.
R12. URL COMPOSITION / '#' EMISSION. f.url is assembled as: scheme-and-authority + path + ('?' + querystr if querystr != '' else '') + ('#' + fragmentstr if fragmentstr != '' else ''). The '?' half of this rule is directly observable: A='http://h/p?#f' -> LINE4 'http://h/p#d?value' (the empty URL query is dropped, no '?'), while A='?q#f' -> '?q#d?value'.
R13. In THIS program LINE4 always contains a '#'. Because LINE3 forces fragment.query = 'value', str(fragment) is never empty, so the '#' is unconditionally emitted. Verified over 126 (A, D) combinations: zero outputs lacked '#'. With D='' the output is exactly '<url>#value' (no path, no '?'), e.g. A='http://h/p' D='' -> 'http://h/p#value'; A='' D='' -> '#value'.
R14. There is NO observable difference between A having a trailing '#' with nothing after it and A having no '#' at all. `--a 'http://h/p'` and `--a 'http://h/p#'` produce byte-identical 4-line output ('', 'c', 'd?value', 'http://h/p#d?value'). Do not track a 'had a fragment delimiter' flag for output purposes.
R15. Empty / degenerate URLs: A='' , A='#', A='?', A='#?', A='?#' all yield LINE4 = '#d?value' (D='d') or '#value' (D=''). A bare '?' with an empty query is dropped from the output; the '#' is still emitted because the fragment is non-empty. Note A='#?' differs from the others in LINE1/LINE2 only ('?' and '?/c'), because its fragment path is the literal '?'.
R16. Adding to the fragment path (LINE2) never affects '#' emission in LINE4, because LINE3 subsequently replaces the whole fragment path with D. Ordering within one run is strictly: parse A -> print (LINE1) -> path.add(C) -> print (LINE2) -> path.load(D) + query.load('value') -> print (LINE3) -> print f.url (LINE4). LINE4 therefore always reflects the LINE3 state of the fragment.
R17. Fragment path join semantics used by add(C) (needed to reproduce LINE2): the result is the existing path segments with C's segments appended, joined by '/'. '' + 'c' -> 'c'; 'a' + 'c' -> 'a/c'; 'a/' + 'c' -> 'a/c' (a trailing empty segment is absorbed); 'a' + 'c/' -> 'a/c/'; '/' + 'c' -> '/c'; 'a' + '' -> 'a'; '' + '' -> ''; '' + '/' -> '/'.
R18. Round-tripping: the output of str(fragment) re-parses to the same (path, query) under the load algorithm. path-only 'a?' re-parses to path 'a?'; query-only 'q=1' re-parses to query 'q=1'; 'a?b=c' re-parses to path 'a', query 'b=c'. The '%3F' escaping in the both-non-empty case is exactly what makes this true.

And reported safe characters: "Fragment PATH (characters emitted literally, from an exhaustive ASCII 33-126 sweep of D and of A's fragment): A-Z a-z 0-9 ! $ & ' ( ) * + , - . / : ; = @ _ ~ — plus '?' ONLY when the fragment query is empty (when the query is non-empty '?' becomes %3F). Percent-encoded in the fragment path: \" -> %22, # -> %23, % -> %25, < -> %3C, > -> %3E, ? -> %3F (query non-empty only), [ -> %5B, \\ -> %5C, ] -> %5D, ^ -> %5E, ` -> %60, { -> %7B, | -> %7C, } -> %7D, space -> %20. In the fragment QUERY, space -> '+' and '?' -> %3F always. The '?' separator itself and the '#' introducer are the only structural characters emitted raw by the composition step."

YOUR JOB: adversarially falsify. For EACH rule, design at least one probe whose outcome the rule predicts, run it against the executable, and compare prediction vs actual. Default to reporting a rule as WRONG or INCOMPLETE if you find any input where it mispredicts. Also hunt for behavior the rules omit entirely (edge cases they never mention). Run at least 50 probes. Return corrections with verbatim observed outputs.

omissions: MAJOR OMISSION - the fragment PATH decoder is PER-SEGMENT ALL-OR-NOTHING, not per-escape. The established-facts line 'furl DECODES percent-escapes on parse and RE-ENCODES on output' is only true when the whole '/'-delimited segment is already a *valid encoded path segment*. Algorithm: split the incoming path text on '/'; for each segment S, S is 'valid encoded' iff every character of S is in the fragment-path safe set (A-Za-z0-9 ! $ & ' ( ) * + , - . : ; = @ _ ~ %) AND every '%' in S is followed by exactly two hex digits. If valid -> percent-DECODE S and store the decoded text. If NOT valid -> store S as literal raw text (no decoding at all). On output each stored segment is percent-encoded with the fragment-path safe set. Segments are judged INDEPENDENTLY. Verbatim (A='#z', varying C, reading LINE2): C='a%2fb'->'z/a%2Fb' (valid, decoded to '/', re-encoded uppercase); C='a%2f b'->'z/a%252f%20b' (space makes the segment invalid, so '%2f' was NOT decoded and its '%' became %25); C='a%2fb%zz'->'z/a%252fb%25zz'; C='%41'->'z/A'; C='%41 '->'z/%2541%20'; C='%41%42'->'z/AB'; C='%41%42 x'->'z/%2541%2542%20x'; C='%41/%zz'->'z/A/%25zz' (per-segment independence: first segment decoded, second not); C='a%20b'->'z/a%20b'; C='a%20 b'->'z/a%2520%20b'; C='%25'->'z/%25'; C='%2541'->'z/%2541'; C='a%'->'z/a%25'; C='a%2'->'z/a%252'. The invalidating character set, found by testing C='%41<ch>' for ch in 32..126 and checking whether '%41' decoded to 'A': space " # % < > ? [ \ ] ^ ` { | } (i.e. exactly the non-safe set, plus '%' when not followed by 2 hex digits). Note '?' is an invalidating character even in the query-empty case where '?' is *output* raw - which is why C='a?b%3Dc' yields '...b%253Dc' and not '...b=c'. Same behaviour for A's fragment path: A='#a%2f b' -> L1='a%252f%20b' vs A='#a%2fb' -> L1='a%2Fb'.

MAJOR OMISSION - the fragment QUERY decoder is the OPPOSITE: per-escape and lenient. Valid escapes are decoded individually and invalid '%' sequences are left as a literal '%' regardless of the rest of the string. Verbatim: A='#?k=%41 b' -> L1='k=A+b' (the '%41' WAS decoded even though a space is present - contrast with the path); A='#?k=%41&j=%zz' -> L1='k=A&j=%25zz'; A='#?k=%2F' -> L1='k=%2F'; A='#?k=%2F b' -> L1='k=%2F+b'; A='#?%41=%42' -> L1='A=B'. So path and query need two DIFFERENT decoders. Do not share code.

OMISSION - TAB (0x09), LF (0x0A) and CR (0x0D) are silently DELETED from A before any parsing (this is Python urlsplit's unsafe-byte removal), everywhere in the URL including inside the fragment; but the same bytes arriving via C or D are percent-encoded normally. Verbatim: A=$'#a\tb' -> L1='ab'; A=$'#a\nb' -> L1='ab'; A=$'#a\rb' -> L1='ab'; A=$'#?k=a\tb' -> L1='k=ab'; A=$'http://h/p\tq#f' -> L4='http://h/pq#d?value'; A=$'http://h/p?a\tb=1#f' -> L4='http://h/p?ab=1#d?value'. But D=$'a\tb' -> L3='a%09b?value' and C=$'a\nb' -> L2='z/a%0Ab'. This also means the deletion happens BEFORE the fragment '?'/'=' split, e.g. A=$'#a\t=b' -> L1='a=b' (parsed as a query). Nearby chars 0x0B and 0x0C are NOT deleted: A=$'#a\x0bb' -> L1='a%0Bb'; A=$'#a\x0cb' -> L1='a%0Cb'.

OMISSION - control and non-ASCII byte handling in the fragment. Control bytes other than 09/0A/0D are percent-encoded with UPPERCASE hex: A=$'#a\x01b' -> L1='a%01b'; D=$'a\x7f' -> L3='a%7F?value'. Non-ASCII is UTF-8 encoded then percent-encoded uppercase, in both path and query: A='#é' -> L1='%C3%A9'; A='#日本' -> L1='%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC'; A='#?k=é' -> L1='k=%C3%A9'; D='é' -> L3='%C3%A9?value'; C='é' -> L2='z/%C3%A9'.

OMISSION - the fragment query preserves pair order, duplicate keys, key-only pairs, empty-value pairs, and leading/trailing/consecutive '&' verbatim. A='#a?z=1&a=2' -> L1='a?z=1&a=2' (NOT sorted); A='#a?b=c&b=d' -> L1='a?b=c&b=d'; A='#a?b=c&' -> L1='a?b=c&'; A='#a?&b=c' -> L1='a?&b=c'; A='#a?&=' -> L1='a?&='; A='#a?=&' -> L1='a?=&'; A='#a?==' -> L1='a?=='; A='#?&&=' -> L1='&&='; A='#a?b&c=d' -> L1='a?b&c=d'; A='#a?b=&c' -> L1='a?b=&c'. Consequence for compose: a non-empty query text NEVER renders as the empty string, so the (non-empty path, empty query) branch of str(fragment) is reachable only when A's fragment had no query part at all.

OMISSION - '#' and its %23 form are indistinguishable after parse: A='#a#b' and A='#a%23b' both give L1='a%23b'. Likewise '?' and '%3F' in D: D='?' and D='%3F' both give L3='%3F?value'. An implementer must decode-then-re-encode rather than pass text through.

OMISSION - exit codes / stderr. Normal runs: rc=0, nothing on stderr. Missing a required option: rc=2, argparse usage on stderr ('usage: test12_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D' then 'test12_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --d'). An unknown option also gives rc=2. No A value I tried (including lone '?', '#', '', '//', control bytes, non-ASCII) caused a non-zero exit.

OUT-OF-AREA OBSERVATION worth flagging to whoever owns scheme/host: the tab/CR/LF deletion does NOT apply to the scheme, which furl appears to extract from the raw string. A=$'htt\tp://h/p#f' -> L4=$'htt\tp://h/p#d?value' - a raw TAB survives in the emitted scheme, and the URL is not re-parsed as http. Contrast A=$'http://h/p\tq#f' -> L4='http://h/pq#d?value'.

COULD NOT DETERMINE - whether the query-empty '?' handling is implemented as encoded_path.replace('%3F','?') (R7's claim) or as 'add ? to the path output safe-set when the query is empty'. I proved the two are observationally EQUIVALENT: the byte sequence '%3F' can only ever be produced by a real '?', because a literal '%' always renders as '%25' (so a decoded segment containing the text '%3F' renders as '%253F', which does not contain the substring '%3F'). Probes: C='%253F' with empty query -> 'a?b/%253F', with non-empty query -> 'z/%253F?q=1'. Either implementation is correct; R7 is not falsifiable here.
